long_biography.plain_text:
José Luis de Federico founded Bizpills in 2002 to develop interactive online training for organisations. As corporate learning moved onto software platforms, the Madrid business introduced a learning-management system, digital courses and tools for creating training content. It gathered those products under the isEazy name, offering companies a connected set of applications rather than a single course library. De Federico was its founder and chief executive through that expansion.

In 2023 private-equity firm ProA Capital acquired a majority stake in the group. De Federico remained as chairman with a stated 20% holding, while Miguel Valverde became chief executive. The transaction reflects the value of a software business he built over two decades, although its undisclosed terms do not establish his personal proceeds or present net worth.
